title: Finite-torsion puncture invariance for a ramified regular divisor tower
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, and let $I=\{n\in\mathbf Z_{>0}:(n,p)=1\}$ be ordered by divisibility. Let $(X_n,h_{mn})_{n\in I}$ be an inverse system of regular Noetherian affine schemes with affine transition morphisms $h_{mn}:X_m\to X_n$ for $n\mid m$, and with $\ell$ invertible on every $X_n$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f_n\in\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ be nonzerodivisors such that $D_n=V(f_n)$ is regular and $h_{mn}^*f_n=f_m^{m/n}$. Write $i_n:D_n\hookrightarrow X_n$, $W_n=X_n[1/f_n]$, and $j_n:W_n\hookrightarrow X_n$; $D_n$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Put $X=\varprojlim_nX_n$, $W=\varprojlim_nW_n=X[1/f_1]$, let $b_n:X\to X_n$ be the projections and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ the principal open immersion [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. All indexing categories and sites are small in compatible universes.

For $s\geq1$ put $A_s=\mathbf Z/\ell^s\mathbf Z$ and use its constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. In the ordinary etale derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] define
$$K_{n,s}=\operatorname{fib}(A_{s,X_n}[0]\longrightarrow Rj_{n,*}A_{s,W_n}[0]),\qquad K_s=\operatorname{fib}(A_{s,X}[0]\longrightarrow Rj_*A_{s,W}[0]),$$
with the actual open adjunction units. Here $\operatorname{fib}(v)=\operatorname{Cone}(v)[-1]$, and $A_s(-1)$ is the dual of the finite Tate line $A_s(1)=\mu_{\ell^s}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Then the normalized supported Cartier Kummer classes of the divisors $D_n$ [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] give derived isomorphisms
$$i_{n,*}A_{s,D_n}(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{n,s}.$$
For $n\mid m$, the morphism $h_{mn}^*K_{n,s}\to K_{m,s}$ is the one induced by the constant-sheaf identification and the open direct-image exchange, the mate of the inverse-image commutative square [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange]. Under the displayed isomorphisms it equals $(m/n)$ times the closed Tate-line exchange, followed by reduction from $V(f_m^{m/n})$ to $V(f_m)$. In particular $\mathcal H^qK_{n,s}=0$ for $q\ne2$, and the transition on $\mathcal H^2$ from $n$ to $n\ell^s\in I$ is zero.

The canonical maps induced by these exchanges give isomorphisms
$$\varinjlim_n b_n^*\mathcal H^q(K_{n,s})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^q(K_s)=0\qquad(q\in\mathbf Z).$$
The actual unit $A_{s,X}[0]\to Rj_*j^*A_{s,X}[0]$ is therefore an isomorphism both in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_s)$ and in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_s)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The pro-etale assertion uses the discrete finite ring $A_s$, ordinary uncompleted derived categories and K-injective total right derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Under the etale-to-pro-etale inverse image it is the same adjunction unit. Empty schemes, empty divisors and identity transitions are permitted; no equality of the schemes $V(f_m^{m/n})$ and $D_m$ is asserted.

proof.text: The poset $I$ is nonempty (it contains $1$) and directed: the product of two positive integers prime to $p$ is a common multiple still prime to $p$. Write $e=m/n$ when $n\mid m$. The equality $h_{mn}^*f_n=f_m^e$ gives $h_{mn}^{-1}(W_n)=W_m$, since an element is invertible exactly when its positive power is invertible. Hence all open squares, including the projection squares at the limit, are Cartesian. Restricting the affine transition maps to these inverse-image opens remains affine (on affine charts it is localization). Each $j_n$ is a principal affine open immersion, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the same is true of $j$. In affine coordinates the colimit of the localized rings is the localization of the colimit ring: a compatible map out of either ring is exactly a compatible family of ring maps inverting $f_1$, equivalently all $f_n$. This verifies $W=\varprojlim W_n=X[1/f_1]$ and the geometric hypotheses for relative continuity.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general: verification of the hypotheses in this principal-open system

proof.text: Apply the existing ramified Cartier supported-purity statement to $X_n,X_m,f_n,f_m,h_{mn}$ and $e=m/n$. Its hypotheses hold verbatim: the two schemes and their divisors are regular Noetherian, both parameters are nonzerodivisors, and $\ell$ is invertible. It gives the Kummer-normalized isomorphisms $P_n:i_{n,*}A_s(-1)[-2]\simeq K_{n,s}$ and the equality $\theta_{mn}h_{mn}^*P_n=P_m(e\rho_{mn})[-2]$, with the actual open-unit exchange and the closed exchange followed by reduction from $V(f_m^e)$ to $V(f_m)$. This proves the finite-stage isomorphism, the specified derived transition formula, and concentration of $K_{n,s}$ in degree $2$. The same statement with $e=1$ gives the identity normalization. No identification of the nonreduced pullback divisor with $D_m$ is made.

source.place: Expose XVI Section 2.1 and Theorem 3.1.1; application of the existing ramification-multiplicity node

proof.text: Exactness of constant-coefficient inverse image, and preservation of homology by an exact functor, identify $\mathcal H^q(b_n^*K_{n,s})$ with $b_n^*\mathcal H^q(K_{n,s})$. Take $m=n\ell^s$; it belongs to $I$ because $p\ne\ell$. Step 2 says the transition in degree $2$ is $\ell^s\rho_{mn}=0$ as an $A_s$-linear map; all other degrees are already zero. Thus every structural map into the colimit of $b_n^*\mathcal H^q(K_{n,s})$ is zero: its cocone relation factors it through this zero transition. By the universal property of a colimit its identity morphism is zero, so this colimit is the zero sheaf. This argument uses vanishing of morphisms, and does not require sections of a sheaf colimit to be sectionwise colimits.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, application after the ramification formula; elementary cocone calculation

proof.text: The long exact cohomology sequence of the fibre triangle $K_{n,s}\to A_{s,X_n}[0]\to Rj_{n,*}A_{s,W_n}[0]$ and Step 2 give that the actual unit $A_{s,X_n}\to j_{n,*}A_{s,W_n}$ is invertible and, for $r\geq1$, give $R^rj_{n,*}A_{s,W_n}\simeq\mathcal H^{r+1}(K_{n,s})$. These are the connecting maps of the fibre triangle. The triangle maps defined by the open exchanges commute with its differentials, so these identifications identify the higher-image transitions with the supported transitions. Consequently $R^1j_{n,*}A_s$ is killed by the transition to $n\ell^s$, and $R^rj_{n,*}A_s=0$ for $r\geq2$. Negative cohomology is zero since right derived direct image of a sheaf is bounded below in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological, applied to the mapping-fibre triangle

proof.text: Apply relative continuity to $u_n=j_n$, with the constant abelian sheaves underlying $A_{s,W_n}$. Step 1 verifies small directed index, affine transitions on both sides, and quasi-compact quasi-separated $j_n$. Their pulled-back coefficient diagram is the constant diagram $A_{s,W}$ with identity maps, so its colimit is $A_{s,W}$. The continuity node gives $\varinjlim b_n^{-1}R^rj_{n,*}A_s\simeq R^rj_*A_s$, with exactly the canonical exchange transitions and legs. Forgetting coefficients identifies these with the module exchanges, since the squares in Step 1 are Cartesian. In degree zero Step 4 identifies the source diagram, including its units, with the constant diagram $A_{s,X}$; its canonical map is therefore the degree-zero unit. In positive degrees the colimit is zero, by Step 4 and the cocone argument of Step 3. Hence the actual unit $A_{s,X}[0]\to Rj_*A_{s,W}[0]$ induces isomorphisms in all degrees. Equivalently its fibre has zero cohomology: the long exact fibre sequence gives $\mathcal H^q(K_s)=0$ for every integer $q$. The canonical maps from Step 3 to these cohomology sheaves are maps between zero sheaves, and hence are isomorphisms. Finally an acyclic representing complex becomes zero in the derived localization, so a map with this acyclic fibre is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, statement and first two paragraphs of proof; actual mate-defined comparison

proof.text:
Use the discrete-ring direct-image comparison with $g=j$ and $K=A_{s,W}[0]$. Its bounded-below hypothesis holds in degree zero; $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1, even though the limit $X$ need not be Noetherian. The isomorphism $
u_X^*Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}A_s\simeq Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_W^*A_s$, together with $j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_X^*\simeq
u_W^*j_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ and constant-sheaf identification, carries the etale unit to the pro-etale unit by its stated unit compatibility. Applying $
u_X^*$ to the isomorphism in Step 5 proves the asserted pro-etale isomorphism in the ordinary uncompleted category, with the same unit. If a divisor is empty its complement is all of the corresponding scheme and its fibre is zero; if a scheme is empty all its module sheaves are zero. These cases also satisfy every preceding argument.
